plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between 0 and 20, the expected value of the highest of the other two bids is approximately (2/3)*20 = 13.33. To account for risk aversion and potential overbidding by others, I will bid slightly higher, but still below my value. I will bid $13.40.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a value of $42, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the other bidders' highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, a reasonable assumption is that other bidders will bid conservatively. To maximize profit, I'll bid a small increment above what I believe the second highest bid will be. I will bid $10.10.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and the auction rules (highest bidder wins, pays the second-highest bid), the optimal strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any deviation downwards risks losing the auction to someone bidding slightly below your value, resulting in a loss when you would have profited. Bidding above your value risks overpaying. My value is $28, so I will bid $28.
